sections.html:
Wilson County splits property tax between two offices, both at 228 East Main Street in downtown Lebanon. The Property Assessor decides value. The Trustee mails the bills and takes payment.

The Trustee is in Room 102, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 865, Lebanon, TN 37088. The phone is 615-444-0894. Press option 1 for real property, tangible personal property and ad valorem tax, or option 2 for the tax freeze, tax relief and benefits for disabled former service members. Hours are Monday through Friday, 8 am to 4 pm. Call the Assessor at 615-444-8661 for questions on value or address.

One detail catches people out. A new mailing address for your tax bill is filed with the Assessor, not the Trustee, by form or by phone.

Lebanon is the seat of Wilson County, in Middle Tennessee east of Nashville, while Mt. Juliet has the most residents. The 2020 census counted 147,737 people and 58,152 housing units, with 75.1% of occupied homes lived in by their owners, and the 2025 estimate is 175,033. Quick growth is built into the values you see. Wilson County Schools runs 22 public schools, and the Lebanon Special School District serves most of Lebanon for grades K to 8.

sections.h2: Due dates and the assessment calendar
sections.html:
Notices are mailed to the property address in mid-October. The tax year follows the calendar year, and you can pay without interest from mid-October to the last day of February. The 2026 bills carry a no-interest window that closes at the end of February 2027.

The roll reaches the Trustee before the first Monday in October, and that is the moment taxes become payable. The calendar below shows the steps leading up to your bill:

Wilson County assessment calendar
DateWhat happens
January 1Assessment date set by state law
By February 1Mailing of business equipment schedules
March 1Return of those schedules; greenbelt applications due
May 20Assessor posts values to the roll and sends change notices
June 1County Board of Equalization starts hearing cases
August 1Last day to appeal to the State Board, or 45 days after the county board's result if that is later
Before first Monday in OctoberRoll is delivered to the Trustee, and taxes turn payable

Payment can reach the Trustee five ways, and the costs differ. Write the tax bill number on a check, or enclose the top portion of the notice.

  • Send a check made out to the Wilson County Trustee to P.O. Box 865, Lebanon, TN 37088.
  • Walk in at 228 E Main Street, Room 102, Lebanon.
  • Pay online through the Tennessee Payments Portal by card or e-check. A card adds a 2.50% fee, which the processor keeps.
  • Phone 1-888-382-8422.
  • Visit a Wilson Bank & Trust or Pinnacle Bank branch in Wilson County between October and February, bill in hand. Banks do not take partial payments.

If your lender holds escrow, the statement you receive is only a copy, because the lender pays the Trustee. After a sale, compare any escrow refund and the buyer's bill against your closing papers.

Go to the Assessor first, by phone or in person. A clerical slip can often be corrected right there. Still unhappy? Request a hearing before the County Board of Equalization, which sits from June 1 each year.

Five property owners serve two-year terms on that board: one from Lebanon, one from Mt. Juliet and three from the county at large. About ten days before it convenes, the Assessor runs a newspaper notice. Slots are booked by phone or in person during the last week of May or first week of June. A family member, attorney or authorized agent may appear for you, or you can go yourself. Arrive about fifteen minutes ahead to complete a form.

The board weighs only whether your value is fair and equitable. Pleas about what you can afford do not count. Results typically go out by mail before June ends, with a letter on how to continue to the State Board of Equalization by August 1 or 45 days after the letter, whichever is later.

Take along nearby sales of comparable houses, photos of defects, and any appraisal or repair quote. Sellers should note that a lower value will not change what a buyer pays for the house, but it does lower the tax the buyer takes on.

sections.h2: Tax relief and the senior freeze
sections.html:
The Trustee administers two programs. Tax Relief assists taxpayers 65 or older, disabled citizens, and totally and permanently disabled former service members. The Tax Freeze program holds the tax on the primary residence of owners 65 and older.

For tax year 2026 the county commission lifted the freeze income limit from $51,790 to $63,470. You meet with Trustee staff, and the back of the bill explains the steps. Applicants usually bring last year's tax return, a driver's license, and Social Security and Medicare cards. The rules cover everyone named on the deed. A frozen amount holds until the next tax year, when the owner must reapply.

A homeowner who qualifies should apply early in the season so the file is complete before the next bill is due. The freeze applies only to your primary residence. Before listing, phone option 2 at 615-444-0894 and ask what changes once the house sells.

Get these answers before you sign a contract, and the closing statement will come out accurate.

  • Ask the Trustee for the current balance on the parcel, and whether earlier years show anything owed.
  • Find out whether the property sits inside Lebanon or Watertown, since those city councils set their own property tax rates.
  • Ask the Assessor whether a change notice or appeal is pending.
  • Learn whether a freeze or relief enrollment is on file in your name.
  • Tell the title company which tax year is unpaid so it can collect from your proceeds.

Closing agents like to see a paid receipt for the most recent year in your file, so keep yours handy and ask the Trustee's office for a printout if the original is lost.

A business run from the home is a separate account. Its tangible personal property schedule is due to the Assessor by March 1 each year, and the county places a forced assessment when none is filed.

A buyer who finances will have a lender that wants taxes current, so unpaid years are usually cleared at the table. A cash sale has no lender review, which removes one source of delay, but the unpaid tax still comes out of the sale money.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Wilson County property taxes?
faqs.a: Pay the Wilson County Trustee at 228 E Main Street, Room 102, Lebanon, by mail, online, by phone at 1-888-382-8422, or at participating banks from October through February. The Trustee's number is 615-444-0894.
You can pay without interest from mid-October through the last day of February. Call the Trustee for the interest schedule that applies after February.

faqs.q: How do I contest my property value?
faqs.a: Contact the Assessor at 615-444-8661 first. If that fails, request a hearing with the County Board of Equalization, which meets starting June 1. A State Board appeal is due by August 1 or 45 days after the county letter.

faqs.q: Is there a tax freeze for seniors?
faqs.a: Yes. The Tax Freeze program fixes the tax on the primary residence of owners 65 and older who meet the income limit, $63,470 for tax year 2026. Apply through the Trustee.
The County Commission sets the county rate. The city councils of Lebanon and Watertown set their own city rates.
